questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests policy-as-code proficiency, practical use of Gatekeeper/OPA, and ability to derive concrete manifests and validation steps for a CNF multi-tenant setup.

## Key Concepts

- OPA Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- ReadOnlyRootFilesystem, hostNetwork, and Privileged security controls
- Namespace-scoped policy targeting CNFs
- Lightweight test manifests to validate allow/deny paths

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (yaml)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: cnfnamespacesecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: CNFNamespaceSecurityConstraint
        listKind: CNFNamespaceSecurityConstraintList
        plural: cnfnamespacesecurityconstraints
        singular: cnfnamespacesecurityconstraint
  targets:
  - target: admissionreviews
    rego: |
      package cnfnamespacesecurity
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        some i
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.hostNetwork
        msg := "hostNetwork is forbidden for CNFs"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        not input.review.object.spec.containers
        # fallback for non-pods
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        some i
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem != true
        msg := "readOnlyRootFilesystem is required for all containers"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.privileged == true
        msg := "privileged containers are disallowed"
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (yaml)
apiVersion: cnfnamespacesecurity.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: CNFNamespaceSecurityConstraint
metadata:
  name: cnf-a-security
spec:
  namespace: cnf-a
```

```yaml
# Compliant Pod (yaml)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-cnf
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
    securityContext:
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      privileged: false
      runAsNonRoot: true
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
```

```yaml
# Non-compliant Pod (yaml)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-cnf
spec:
  hostNetwork: true
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
    securityContext:
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: false
      privileged: true
```

## Follow-up Steps

- Apply ConstraintTemplate, Constraint, and test manifests in a single namespace and observe denial events for non-compliant pods.
- Extend with a quick kubectl patch to simulate remediation and re-validate.

```javascript
// Pseudo: evaluatePolicy(tenant, method, path) -> boolean
function evaluatePolicy(tenant, method, path) {
  const rules = policy[tenant] || []
  for (const r of rules) {
    if (r.method === method && (r.path === path || matches(r.path, path))) return true
  }
  return false
}
```

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests the ability to design tenant-isolated API validation using per-tenant OpenAPI specs, driven by a request header, within a CNF gateway. It emphasizes practical config storage, request validation, error handling, and observability.

## Key Concepts

- Per-tenant OpenAPI specs stored in ConfigMaps
- Tenant selection via X-TENANT-ID header
- Lightweight JSON validation using Ajv or similar
- Structured error responses (400) with detailed validation messages
- Audit logging for security and debugging
- Namespace-scoped manifests for isolation

## Code Example

```javascript
// Pseudo-validator flow:
// 1. Extract X-TENANT-ID header from request
// 2. Load corresponding OpenAPI spec from cnf.api.spec ConfigMap
// 3. Compile Ajv validator from spec
// 4. Validate request body and headers against schema
// 5. Return 400 with structured error if validation fails
// 6. Pass through to upstream service if valid
```

## Minimal YAML

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf.api.spec
data:
  tenant-a.yaml: |-
    openapi: 3.0.0
    paths:
      /api/resource:
        post:
          requestBody:
            required: true
            content:
              application/json:
                schema:
                  type: object
                  required: [name]
                  properties:
                    name:
                      type: string
          responses:
            '200':
              description: Success
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: api-gateway
spec:
  selector:
    app: gateway
  ports:
    - port: 8080
      targetPort: 8080
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-gateway
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: gateway
          image: nginx:1.21
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          volumeMounts:
            - name: spec-config
              mountPath: /etc/cnf-specs
              readOnly: true
        - name: validator-sidecar
          image: validator:latest
          env:
            - name: SPEC_PATH
              value: /etc/cnf-specs
          volumeMounts:
            - name: spec-config
              mountPath: /etc/cnf-specs
              readOnly: true
      volumes:
        - name: spec-config
          configMap:
            name: cnf.api.spec
```

```yaml
# Example 1: Deployment rolling update strategy
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment

      maxSurge: 1

        app: gateway
        version: v1.y

      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: gateway:v1.y
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
        readinessProbe:

            port: 8443
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 5
        env:
```
